source: OBR, Economic and fiscal outlook, October 2026: Annex A and the detailed forecast tables (economy, receipts)
replaces: OBR EFO March 2026, as shipped in policyengine-uk 2.151.0 (gov.economic_assumptions.yoy_growth.obr)
applies_to: Every simulation the dashboard builds, baseline and reform alike (uk_budget_data.forecast.with_forecast). Applied before data load, so the dataset's projected years follow it.
notes: Growth rates are calendar years 2026 to 2031, keyed YYYY-01-01.YYYY-12-31 and applied before data load. CPI, RPI, CPIH, average earnings and rents are the economy detailed forecast tables' Tables 1.6 and 1.7 at four decimals, read as policyengine-uk's import_obr_forecasts reads them (the source of the engine's own March values); they equal Table A.1 to one decimal. House prices are Table A.1, as the engine cites. 2025 is outturn and is left as shipped (the October tables revise some 2025 figures, e.g. earnings 5.3% to 4.1%); after 2031 the engine's long-run path is kept.

Statutory uprating inputs keep their published outturns (September 2026 CPI 3.5%, May-July 2026 earnings 3.9%). Their forecast years are calendar-year growth plus forecast_gap, recomputed from the October tables as import_obr_forecasts does: September CPI from receipts Table 4.19, May-July earnings from Table 1.6's Q2 growth. Every Table A.3 triple-lock figure is reproduced (tests/test_forecast_basis.py).

Per-capita series (GDP, mixed income, non-labour income) are aggregate growth minus ons.population growth (the engine's March 2025 vintage), as the engine derives them: nominal GDP from Table A.1, mixed and non-labour income from Table 1.12.
consumer_price_index_ahc is recomputed by policyengine-uk's create_ahc_deflator from the October CPI and rents (and Ofwat water bills, unchanged).

Fuel duty (gov.hmrc.fuel_duty.petrol_and_diesel), added in code (uk_budget_data.forecast.fuel_duty_rpi_steps): current law is the OBR's 60.59p from April 2027 (EFO paragraph 3.19), then each 1 April the previous calendar year's RPI from this file. The baseline and the fuel duty measure both read this one path.

Carer's Allowance earnings limit (gov.dwp.carers_allowance.earnings_limit), added in code (uk_budget_data.forecast.carers_allowance_earnings_limits): current law is 16 hours at each April's National Living Wage, rounded up to the pound (EM to SI 2025/352, paragraph 5.6), on the OBR wage path the Carer's Allowance taper reads: £212, £217, £222, £228 and £234 a week from 2027-28 to 2031-32. policyengine-uk 2.151.0 holds £204. The baseline and the taper both read this one path.

Not updated: road_fuel_volume and the petrol/diesel spending litre proxies (the engine derives volume from the OBR's fuel duty receipts net of non-road fuel, over fiscal-year average duty rates; receipts Table 4.8 is the cash-basis total, and with the March receipts tables unavailable here the method cannot be checked against the engine's March values, so it is left for policyengine-uk's importer), and ons.population (a March 2025 vintage the engine keeps by choice). They keep the March 2026 path.
